confidence: high on the domain fact, medium on the index attribution (see residual_uncertainty)

evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

what_the_scenario_name_pins.the_120: Splinters of Wrath = 120, the cap of Syndra's Transcendent passive. Confirmed independently by data/champions.json ('stacking up to 120 times', 'At 120 Splinters of Wrath ... increasing her ability power by 15%') and by data/champion-audit/batch-6.json ('splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP buff').
what_the_scenario_name_pins.custom_order: the fight runs a caller-supplied cast order rather than the DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER (fixed Q,W,E,R) described in data/worklists/f2-task.md. The order itself is not recoverable from data/ — see residual_uncertainty.

independent_computation.question_restated: Which ability legitimately owns the 10th (0-indexed 9th) damage event of a Syndra fight at 120 Splinters of Wrath?

step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.reasoning: The number and identity of damage events per cast is fixed by the cached wiki text for each slot at 120 splinters. Enumerating it bounds which sources can appear where.
step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.Q_Dark_Sphere: 1 magic event per cast, BUT effect[1]: 'Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.' 120 >= 40 -> 2 stocked Q casts -> 2 Q events in a burst.
step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.W_Force_of_Will: effect[2] recast deals 'magic damage'; effect[3]: 'Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath enhances Force of Will to deal 12% (+ 2% per 100 AP) bonus TRUE damage.' 120 >= 60 -> a W cast at this splinter count carries TWO damage packets of DIFFERENT damage types -> 2 W events.
step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.E_Scatter_the_Weak: 1 magic event (the 80-splinter bonus is scatter-angle + slow, i.e. CC only - no extra damage instance).
step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.R_Unleashed_Power: 'conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones', 'Magic Damage per Sphere' -> 3..7 per-sphere events (the audit notes R reads per-sphere damage x a user-set sphere count). The 100-splinter execute is documented not modeled.
step_1_event_inventory_at_120_splinters.P_Transcendent: no damage event: 'At 120 Splinters of Wrath ... increasing her ability power by 15%' is a buff, not a damage instance.

step_2_the_W_true_damage_packet_is_real_.claim: At >=60 splinters a single W cast MUST author two damage events, not one.
step_2_the_W_true_damage_packet_is_real_.why_two_events_not_one: The bonus is TRUE damage while the base is MAGIC damage. docs/math-foundations.md pins mitigation as a per-packet, per-resistance operator - 'Resistance mitigation (apply_resistance) | m(R)=100/(100+R)' with 'True damage ignores all resistances entirely' (CLAUDE.md domain rules). m(R) is linear in raw damage for a FIXED resistance ('Multi-hit abilities ... exact because the mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R) is linear in raw damage for a fixed resistance'), so packets may be merged ONLY when they share a resistance. A magic packet and a true packet do not, so they cannot be collapsed into one event without corrupting the mitigation.
step_2_the_W_true_damage_packet_is_real_.arithmetic_check: I re-derived the wiki's own 'Bonus True Damage' rows from the prose formula and reproduced them exactly. With base magic per rank B = [70,100,130,160,190] and 65% AP ratio, bonus true = (0.12 + 0.0002*AP) * (B + 0.65*AP) expands to: constant 0.12*B = [8.4, 12, 15.6, 19.2, 22.8] (cached row: [8.4, 12, 15.6, 19.2, 22.8] - MATCH); AP coefficient 0.12*0.65 + 0.0002*B = [9.2, 9.8, 10.4, 11.0, 11.6] %AP (cached row: [9.2, 9.8, 10.4, 11, 11.6] %AP - MATCH); AP-squared coefficient 0.0002*0.65 = 1.30e-4, which the wiki encodes as the product of two '% AP' units, sqrt(1.30e-4) = 0.01140 = 1.14 %AP (cached row: [1.14 ...] with units ['% AP','% AP'] - MATCH). The cached 'Total Mixed Damage' row [78.4, 112, 145.6, 179.2, 212.8] = B + 0.12*B confirms the wiki itself models the cast as magic + true summed, i.e. two components.
step_2_the_W_true_damage_packet_is_real_.concrete_scenario_numbers: At the corpus-standard fight tuple used throughout data/worklists (level 18, rank 5, R rank 3, no items -> AP = 0, so the 120-splinter x1.15 AP buff contributes 0): W magic = 190, W bonus true = 22.8, total mixed = 212.8 - exactly the cached rank-5 'Total Mixed Damage' constant. Q rank 5 = 230 (+70% AP) per charge, x2 charges at 120 splinters.

step_3_index_transition_analysis.observation: A single leaf flipping Q -> W at index 9 is the signature of an INSERTION into the event stream immediately before a Q (new[9] = the inserted event, old[9] = Q slides to new[10]) or of an insertion one slot earlier (new[9] = old[8] = W). Both readings are insertions, not relabelings.
step_3_index_transition_analysis.which_insertions_are_licensed_at_120_spl: Exactly the two the wiki grants at this splinter count and at no lower one: (a) the W bonus-true-damage packet (unlocked at 60), and (b) the second stocked Dark Sphere charge (unlocked at 40). Under reading (a) the inserted event IS the W true packet and index 8 is the W magic packet. Under reading (b) a Q2 event is inserted earlier and new[9] = old[8], which the transition requires to be a W event. Either way the value that correctly lands on index 9 is a W-sourced event.
step_3_index_transition_analysis.worked_consistency_check: A concrete stream that reproduces both observed values exactly, using the reversed-default custom order R,E,W,Q with the maximum 7 spheres ('conjures 3 ... and additionally grabs up to 4'): old (W as one packet) = [R,R,R,R,R,R,R, E, W, Q, Q] -> index 9 = Q; new (W as magic+true) = [R x7, E, W_magic, W_true, Q, Q] -> index 9 = W. The single wiki-mandated insertion reproduces the whole observed change; no other edit is needed.
step_3_index_transition_analysis.what_would_make_the_OLD_value_right: Only a DELETION of a legitimate earlier event (shifting the tail left so new[9] = old[10] = W) - i.e. the engine dropping either the second Q charge or the W true packet. Both deletions are forbidden by the cached wiki text at 120 splinters ('40 Splinters ... stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2'; '60 Splinters ... bonus true damage'). So the old stream can only be right if the new one dropped something, and nothing is droppable at 120.

independent_computation.conclusion: The 120-splinter variant is precisely the configuration in which Syndra's stream gains extra damage events (2nd Q charge at 40, W true packet at 60), and a lone Q -> W flip at one index is the shape those insertions produce. The new value is the one consistent with the cached wiki text.

sources_quoted.quote: Innate: Syndra collects Splinters of Wrath that enhance each of her abilities based on the number of them collected, stacking up to 120 times.
At 120 Splinters of Wrath, Syndra achieves Transcendence, increasing her ability power by 15%.
Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 40 Splinters of Wrath causes Syndra to periodically stock a Dark Sphere charge, up to a maximum of 2.
Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath enhances Force of Will to deal 12% (+ 2% per 100 AP) bonus true damage.
Recast: Syndra throws the grabbed target towards the target location ... dealing magic damage to them and nearby enemies once they land.

Active: Syndra conjures 3 Dark Spheres and additionally grabs up to 4 nearby live ones. Afterwards, she barrages the target enemy champion with all collected Dark Spheres, each dealing magic damage upon hit.
splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP buff; R reads 'Magic Damage per Sphere' x user-set sphere count.
E3 implemented the Transcendent splinter system (splinters option: 120 -> 1.15x AP buff, 40+ Q charges via Q2 slot, 60+ W true damage), R sphere count (r_spheres).

A part with h identical hits is mitigated per hit and summed: sum_h m(R)*raw = h*m(R)*raw (_mitigate_hits). This is exact because the mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R) is linear in raw damage for a fixed resistance.
Resistance mitigation (apply_resistance) | m(R)=100/(100+R); EHP round-trip raw = post*(1+R/100) | EXACT
src/calculator/damage.py computes a rotation from a DEFAULT_CAST_ORDER (fixed Q,W,E,R) ... The event order shown in the UI comes from the fight's cast_order + breakdown damage_events.

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'syndra_custom_order_120' lives outside the permitted evidence tree (scripts/ and tests/ are off-limits under R-18/R-19), so the exact custom cast order, r_spheres value, auto-attack count and fight window could not be read. The index-9 reconstruction in step 3 is therefore an existence proof (a wiki-consistent stream that reproduces both the old and the new value) rather than a unique derivation.

The verdict does not depend on that reconstruction: it rests on the direction of the change. A lone Q -> W flip is an insertion signature, every insertion licensed at 120 splinters (2nd Q charge, W true packet) is mandated by the cached wiki text, and the only transition that would make the OLD value right is a deletion of an event that 120 splinters forbids deleting.

Not ruled out by data/ alone: that index 9 should hold some third source entirely (an R sphere or an auto) under a different custom order. Nothing in the cached data suggests it, so 'both_wrong' is unsupported.
